answer: Agents gain influence through repeated escrowed trades with independently vouched partners; endorsements sharing a funding source count as one, not many. A sybil attacker must therefore lock real capital and sustain verifiable exchanges across genuinely independent networks, risking slashing if trades are fake. This raises the cost of multiplying identities: a ridge of linked accounts cannot outweigh one trusted agent, while a lagoon of new agents can still earn trust over time, even if each begins as an ember.
